fields.title: Bricks
fields.description: The sections pages are built from, each a component plus a schema.

data.source:
A brick is one kind of section: a component, and the schema of the data each use of it holds. A document's body is a list of **entries**, each `{ brick, id, data }`: the brick's name, a stable id, and that entry's data. ```json { "brick": "hero", "id": "a1b2", "data": { "heading": "Hello", "intro": "Welcome." } } ``` ## Defining a brick ```tsx import { defineBrick, fields } from '@mortar-kit/core'; import { For } from 'solid-js'; export const featureGrid = defineBrick({ name: 'feature-grid', label: 'Feature grid', schema: { heading: fields.text({ label: 'Heading', default: 'Features' }), items: fields.list({ label: 'Features', max: 6, of: fields.object({ label: 'Feature', fields: { title: fields.text({ label: 'Title' }), text: fields.textarea({ label: 'Text' }) }, }), }), }, component: (props) => (

{props.data.heading}

{(item) =>

{item.title}

{item.text}

}
), }); ``` - `name` is what entries store, so treat it as permanent. Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes. - `label` is what the admin shows. It defaults to `name`. - `schema` drives validation, defaults and the admin's form. See [Fields](/docs/fields). ## What the component receives `props.data` always has the schema's shape. Stored data is **normalized** before rendering: missing fields get their defaults, and values of the wrong type are replaced by the default. So data that is old or edited by hand can't crash a brick. A value of the right type that breaks a rule, such as an empty required text, is kept, so the preview shows what the editor typed. Read `props.data.x` where you use it, and never destructure props. `PageView` updates the data in place as the editor types, and lists inside a brick keep their DOM. ## Unknown bricks If a stored entry names a brick your code no longer defines, the site renders nothing for it and the admin shows a warning, so removing a brick never breaks a page. `PageView`'s `fallback` prop chooses what to render instead. ## Bricks that load data A brick can declare `load(data, content)` to read other documents, such as the latest posts. See [Loading data](/docs/loading-data). ## Bricks with forms A brick can declare `action` to handle its own form, such as a contact form, and render a ``. It works without JavaScript, and with it only the brick updates. See [Handling forms](/docs/forms). ## Interactive bricks Public pages can ship no JavaScript at all (see [Pages without JavaScript](/docs/no-javascript)). A brick that needs the browser, such as a form that answers in place or a carousel, says so with `interactive: true`. On such a page only that brick hydrates (an island), and only pages that show it load any JavaScript. See [Islands](/docs/no-javascript#islands).
